lines.text: On the morning of the final, I went to Wren's tent.
You don't have to win this, Wren.
Yes, I do. The winner asks the King for one thing. I'm asking for you. And a horse. A good one.
Tamsin was in the Lowmarket with Hobb that morning, mapping the tunnels. Later, I thanked every god I don't believe in.
The final of the King's Tourney! Brother Caddoc, of the Order of the Measure! Ember! Six rings!
Six milky stones across the knuckles of his gauntlets. Bought, every one. They burned exactly as hot as real ones.
Wren fought him the way Oswin had taught her. Hold the rings in. Stay small. Stay fast. Watch the left.
It wasn't enough. His fire filled the ring from wall to wall. There was nowhere left to be small in.
So Wren stopped holding back.
The wind rose around her like a living thing. Four rings, blazing. Nearly five. The court gasped. A peasant girl from the north, lit like a knight-captain.
Her arrow came within a finger of Caddoc's throat. He caught it in his gauntlet, and it burned.
Then his fire came down on her like a falling wall. Her bowstring burned through. She went down, and she didn't get up.
Yield, girl.
No.
The marshal called it for her. Wren of Greyhollow could not continue. Brother Caddoc had won the King's Tourney.
My boon, Majesty. You all saw that peasant. Four rings, in a commoner. The zero's whole household shines like her. I ask for all of them. To the Order, for questioning.
Uncle, this is a farce.
King Edric looked at the Grand Measurer before he answered. He always did.
Granted.
The Hounds came into the stands. They took Wren off the sand, and Corvin from his seat. Oswin was too burned to move, so they left him.
Ash rose up beside me with his lips drawn back. I put my hand on his neck.
Ash. Down.
It was the hardest order I have ever given. If he fought, they would have their excuse.
Then the Grand Measurer came down from the royal box himself, to a quiet woman in a grey dress, and took off her square spectacles.
Square spectacles, Ilse? You always did have a sense of humour.
Lucan. Don't come for me.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter ninety-one, coming soon.
